title: Day 3 Teaching Lab — Access Decision and Investigation Chain
objective: Study-guide review — Day 3 — Zero Trust, IAM, Endpoint, and Network Engineering: Day 3 Teaching Lab — Access Decision and Investigation Chain.

blocks.text: Scenario: a contractor uses a personal laptop from a new location to access a source-code repository. The login succeeds. Minutes later, endpoint logs from a build server show unusual script execution, DNS logs show unfamiliar lookups, and IAM logs show a privileged role being assumed by a service account.
Ask students to build a single timeline:

rows: Was conditional access applied? Was the device trusted?
Was authorization appropriate for subject, object, and context?
Is this authorized automation or attacker TTP?
Is this normal dependency access or command-and-control signal?
Was PIM or cloud IAM trust policy involved?

items: Zero Trust requires continuous evaluation, not only successful login.
IAM investigation must separate authentication, authorization, and accounting.
Endpoint telemetry explains what ran; network telemetry explains where it connected.
DNS and IAM logs provide context for lateral movement or service misuse.
Containment must account for business impact and evidence preservation.

blocks.text: Wrong-answer discussion: "block the user" may be necessary, but it is not enough. The investigation still needs device posture, access path, service account trust, endpoint process evidence, and network evidence.
Source: CertMaster Study Lessons 3E, 3F, 4A, and 4B; SecurityX M03-M04 slides.
